content.value_statement: Vector search tuning can waste memory and hide recall regressions. This skill gives practical benchmarks, parameter guidance, and monitoring checks for production indexes.
actual_capabilities: Guides index type selection by vector count and performance target.
Recommends HNSW parameter ranges for recall, latency, and build time.
Provides benchmark templates for recall, latency, memory, and QPS measurement.
Compares scalar, product, binary, FP16, and FP32 quantization tradeoffs.
Shows Qdrant collection configuration patterns for recall, speed, balanced, and memory goals.
Defines monitoring metrics for p50, p95, p99 latency, recall, and throughput.
limitations: It needs representative queries and ground truth to validate recall.
It does not design a complete RAG or ranking system.
Examples require adaptation before use with a production vector database.
It does not replace load testing under real traffic.

use_cases.title: Select Production Index Settings
use_cases.description: Choose HNSW and quantization settings that match recall, latency, memory, and build-time targets.

use_cases.title: Plan Benchmark Sweeps
use_cases.description: Create a repeatable benchmark plan for parameter sweeps using real queries and ground truth.

use_cases.title: Control Vector Memory Costs
use_cases.description: Estimate memory use and evaluate compression strategies before scaling vector collections.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Starting Configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner tuning with known dataset size
prompt_templates.prompt: Pick a starting index configuration for <number> vectors with <dimensions> dimensions. Target <recall> recall, <latency> milliseconds, and <memory> GB memory.

prompt_templates.title: Compare HNSW Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare HNSW parameter options for my workload: <vectors>, <dimensions>, <QPS>, <recall target>, and <latency target>. Explain tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Benchmark Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a benchmark plan for vector index tuning using real queries, ground truth, and staging data. Include metrics and rollout gates.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Qdrant Tuning Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Qdrant tuning plan for recall, speed, and memory risk: <plan>. Identify likely regressions and safer alternatives.

output_examples.input: Need 95 percent recall for 2 million 768-dimensional vectors with 12 GB memory.
output_examples.output: Start with HNSW, M near 32, efSearch near 128, and scalar quantization. Validate recall before reducing memory further.

output_examples.input: Current search is fast but recall dropped after quantization.
output_examples.output: Check ground truth recall, enable rescoring, raise oversampling, and compare against an unquantized baseline before rollout.

output_examples.input: Memory use is too high for 50 million vectors.
output_examples.output: Estimate storage by precision, test product quantization, and consider disk-backed segments only after measuring p95 latency.

best_practices: Benchmark with real queries and representative ground truth before changing production settings.
Track recall, latency percentiles, QPS, build time, and memory for every tuning run.
Roll out index changes through staging with rollback and comparison against a baseline.
anti_patterns: Tuning parameters without a baseline or success target.
Optimizing latency while ignoring recall loss.
Reindexing production collections without staged validation or rollback.

faq.question: What vector databases does this skill cover?
faq.answer: The examples include HNSW concepts and Qdrant configuration patterns. The tuning principles also apply to similar vector search systems.

faq.question: Can it choose exact parameter values?
faq.answer: It can suggest starting ranges. Final values require benchmarks with your data, queries, and latency goals.

faq.question: Does it automate benchmarking?
faq.answer: No. It provides benchmark templates and measurement plans that you run in your own environment.

faq.question: When should I use quantization?
faq.answer: Use quantization when memory or cost is a constraint. Measure recall loss before enabling it broadly.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What inputs should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide vector count, dimensions, target recall, latency budget, QPS, memory budget, and representative query sets.
